editorial_note: Nine commentary entries previously marked “No commentary” were restored from the pinned Śrīdhara source. Their phrase-level glosses and continuous literal renderings have been added; the remaining no-commentary labels are source checked. Independent line-by-line review and live-render verification remain pending.
scope: Complete source-bound Śrīdhara commentary for Canto 11 Chapter 6, verses 11.6.1–11.6.50; source groups 11.6.2–11.6.3, 11.6.21–11.6.22, 11.6.37–11.6.38, 11.6.40–11.6.41, and 11.6.48–11.6.49. Nine misclassified passages have been restored; explicit no-commentary markers are retained for the remaining fourteen source ranges.

entries.sanskrit: षष्ठे ब्रह्मादिभिः स्तुत्वा गन्तुं विज्ञापितं हरिम् । उद्धवः प्रार्थयाम् आस स्व-धाम नय माम् इति ॥ अतः परम् अतिविस्तरेणात्म-विद्यां निरूपयितुं तत्-प्रस्तावम् आह---अथेति । आत्मजैः सनकादिभिः । अभ्यगात् द्वारकाम् इति चतुर्थेनान्वयः ॥१॥
word_for_word: having been praised by Brahmā and the others
take me to Your own abode
with the mind-born sons beginning with Sanaka
entries.literal_english: In the sixth chapter, after Brahmā and the others praise the Lord and request His departure, Uddhava asks Him, “Take me to Your own abode.” The account then opens into a detailed teaching on the Self; the sons of Brahmā beginning with Sanaka accompany the approach to Dvārakā.

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.literal_english: No commentary

entries.sanskrit: ननु तेषाम् उपेन्द्रादि-रूपं भगवन्तं नित्यं पश्यतां केयम् अति-दिदृक्षा अत आह---वपुषेति । येन वपुषा नर-लोक-मनोरमः सन् सर्व-लोकेषु यशो वितेने तद् अतिसुन्दरं वपुर् दिदृक्षवः ॥५॥
word_for_word: an especially intense desire to see
removing the impurity of all worlds
entries.literal_english: Although the gods constantly behold the Lord in forms such as Upendra, they still desire to see the particular form that delights the human world and spreads fame which removes the impurity of all worlds.

entries.sanskrit: व्यचक्षत अपश्यन् ॥५॥
entries.literal_english: The source glosses व्यचक्षत simply as “they saw.”

entries.sanskrit: स्वर्गोद्यान-स्थैर् माल्यैः । चित्राणि शृङ्खला-बन्ध-प्रायाणि पदान्य् अर्थाश् च यासु ताभिर् गीर्भिः ॥६॥
word_for_word: with garlands from the gardens of heaven
चित्राणि शृङ्खला-बन्ध-प्रायाणि पदान्य् अर्थाश् च यासु
in which the words and meanings are varied and linked like a chain
entries.literal_english: They adorned the foremost of the Yadus with garlands from the gardens of heaven and praised the Lord of the universe with hymns whose words and meanings were varied and intricately linked.

entries.sanskrit:
बुद्धीन्द्रियादिभिर् दर्शनादिना प्राणेन च बल-हेतुना दण्ड-वत्-प्रणिपातेन नता वयं नमस्-कृतवन्तः । स्मेति विस्मये । यथाहुः---

> दोर्भ्यां पदाभ्यां जानुभ्याम् उरसा शिरसा दृशा । >
> मनसा वचसा चेति प्रणामोऽष्टाङ्ग ईरितः ॥ इति ।

स्म-शब्दोक्त-विस्मयाय विशेषणम् । कर्म-मयाद् उरु-पाशान् मुमुक्षुभिर् भाव-युक्तैर् अपि यत् केवलम् अन्तर्-हृदि चिन्त्यते न तु दृश्यते तद् वयं नताः । अहो भाग्यम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥७॥
word_for_word: through the intellect and senses, by seeing and the other acts
and by the life-breath, the source of strength
दोर्भ्यां पदाभ्यां जानुभ्याम् उरसा शिरसा दृशा
with the arms, feet, knees, chest, head, and eyes
and with the mind and speech: this is called the eight-limbed prostration
from the great bonds made of karma
even by seekers of liberation endowed with devotional feeling
यत् केवलम् अन्तर्-हृदि चिन्त्यते न तु दृश्यते
which is only contemplated within the heart, but is not seen
the meaning is: “Ah, what good fortune!”
entries.literal_english: “We bowed; we paid homage” means that they prostrated themselves, using intellect and senses, seeing and the other acts, and the life-breath that gives strength, as one falls like a staff. The particle sma expresses wonder. The cited verse describes the eight-limbed prostration: arms, feet, knees, chest, head, eyes, mind, and speech. The word sma marks that wonder. Even seekers of liberation who have devotional feeling can only contemplate within the heart—and do not see—the Lord’s feet that release them from karma’s great bonds. “We have bowed to those feet”: ah, what good fortune!

entries.sanskrit: ननु ममापि दृष्टादृष्ट-कर्म-करणात् कुतो मत्-पदारविन्द-चिन्तनं कर्म-पाशान् मुमुक्षुभिः क्रियते ? तत्राहुः---त्वम् इति । हे अजित ! आस्ताम् इदानीन्तनम् इदम् अत्यल्पं कर्म, त्वं व्यक्तं महद्-आदि-प्रपञ्चं सृजसि पालयसि संहरसि च तद् अप्य् आत्मन्य् एवं न पृथक् । दुर्विभव्यं मनसाप्य् अवितर्क्यम् । तद् गुण-स्थस् तस्या मायाया गुणेषु नियन्तृत्वेन स्थितः । अत एव तैः कर्मभिर् भवान् नाज्यते न लिप्यते । कुतः ? यो भवान् अनवद्यो रागादि-रहितः । यतः स्वे आत्म-रूपे सुखेऽव्यवहितेऽनावृते अभिरतः । अतस् त्वं कर्म कुर्वन्न् अप्य् आत्मारामः परमेश्वर इति मुमुक्षुभिश् चिन्त्यस इति भावः ॥८॥
word_for_word: from performing seen and unseen actions
by the māyā of three guṇas
You are contemplated by seekers of liberation
entries.literal_english: The gods ask how one who performs ordinary actions can contemplate the Lord's feet. He creates, maintains, and dissolves the manifest universe through three-guṇa māyā, yet it is not separate from His Self and He remains unstained. Because He is free from attachment and absorbed in unobstructed bliss, seekers of liberation contemplate Him as the actionless Lord.

entries.sanskrit: नन्व् आत्मारामस्य किं कर्म-करणेन ? अत आहुः---शुद्धिर् इति । हे ईड्य ! हे ऋषभ ! दुराशयानां रागिणाम् । विद्या उपासना । विद्यादिभिस् तथा शुद्धिर् न भवति । सत्त्वात्मनां सतां ते यशसि श्रवणेन संभृतया परिपुष्टया अभिवृद्धया सच्-छ्रद्धया यथा स्यात् । परम-पावनस्य यशसो वितानाय तव कर्माचरणम् इति भावः ॥९॥
word_for_word: of one who delights in the Self
through learning, Vedic study, charity, austerity, and ritual acts
through growing pure faith in Your fame
entries.literal_english: Why would the Self-delighting Lord perform actions? The commentary answers that ritual learning and austerity do not purify people of evil desire as effectively as growing pure faith in the Lord's fame, nourished by hearing. His actions are for spreading that supremely purifying fame.

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवं त्वद्-यशः-श्रद्धैव शुद्धि-हेतुः, अस्माभिस् तु तवाङ्घ्रिर् दृष्टोऽतस् तवाङ्घ्रिर्नोऽस्माकम् अशुभाशयानां विषय-वासनानां धूम-केतुस् तद्-दाहकः स्यात् । कथं भूतः ? यः क्षेमाय मोक्षाय मुनिभिर् मुमुक्षुभिः प्रेम्आर्द्र-हृदा ऊह्यमानश् चिन्त्यमानः । यश् च सात्वतैर् भक्तैः सम-विभूतये समानैश्वर्याय वासुदेवादि-व्यूहेऽर्चितः । तेषु च कैश्चिद् आत्म-वद्भिर् धीरैः स्वर्-अतिक्रमाय स्वर्गम् अतिक्रम्य वैकुण्ठ-प्राप्तये सवनशस् त्रि-कालम् अर्चितः ॥१०॥
word_for_word: a comet that burns evil intentions
entries.literal_english: The Lord's feet burn away the evil tendencies of devotees. Sages longing for liberation contemplate them; Sātvatas worship them for divine majesty; and self-possessed devotees worship them three times daily to pass beyond heaven and attain Vaikuṇṭha.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, प्रयत-पाणिभिः संयत-हस्तैर् हविर् गृहीत्वाध्वराग्नौ आहवनीयादौ याज्ञिकैर् यश् चिन्त्यते । ननु, यस्यै देवतायै हविर् गृहीतं स्यात् तां ध्यायेद् वषट् करिष्यन् इति वचनात् तत्-तद्-देवताश् चिन्त्यन्ते अत आहुः---त्रय्या निरुक्तेन विधिनेन्द्रादि-रूपेणैव यज्ञ-पुरुषश् चिन्त्यत इत्य् अर्थः । उत किं च । अध्यात्म-योगे आत्माधिकारे योगे योगिभिर् अप्य् आत्मनस् तव माया अणिमादिस् तां जिज्ञासुभिस् तत् तत् कामैर् यश् चिन्त्यते । परम-भागवतैस् तु मुक्तैर् यः परीष्टः सर्वतः पूजितः स तवाङ्घ्रिर् नोऽशुभाशय-धूमकेतुः स्याद् इति पूर्वेणान्वयः ॥११॥
word_for_word: by the procedure explained in the three Vedas
in the yoga concerning the Self
by those desiring to know His māyā
entries.literal_english: Sacrificers take the oblation with controlled hands and meditate on the Lord as the Person of sacrifice according to the three Vedas. Yogins contemplate His māyā while seeking its powers. Desireless supreme devotees, however, worship His feet everywhere and at all times for liberation.

entries.sanskrit: एतेषां च मुनि-सात्वतादीनां षण्णां सेवकानां मध्ये परम-भागवतेषु लक्ष्म्या अपि तव प्रीतिर् अधिकेति संस्तुवन्ति---पर्युष्टयेति । इड-भावश् छान्दसः । अहं यत्र वसामि, तत्रैव वक्षसि पर्युषितापीयं वसतीति प्रतिपत्निवत् सपत्नीवच् छ्रीः संस्पर्धमाना भवति । तथापि स्पर्धमानां श्रियम् अनादृत्य यो भवान् पर्युषितयापि अमुया वन-मालया भक्तैर् अर्पितेयम् इति प्रीत्या सुप्रणीतं सुष्ठु सम्पादितं यथा भवति, तथार्हणं पूजाम् आददत् स्वीकृतवान् । सुप्रणीतम् इत्य् अर्हण-विशेषणं वा । तस्य तवाङ्घ्रिर् नोऽशुभाशय-धूमकेतुर् भूयात् । यद् वा, योऽङ्घ्रिर् अमुया सुप्रणीतम् अर्हणम् आददत्, स नोऽशुभाशय-धूमकेतुर् भूयाद् इत्य् अन्वयः । अथवैवं संबन्धः, एतेभ्यो ध्यानार्चनादि-निष्ठेभ्योऽपि त्वद्-यशसि प्रवृद्ध-सच्-छ्रद्धावन्त एव कृतार्थः । भगवतो यशः-प्रियत्वाद् इत्य् आहुः---पर्युष्टया । "वश कान्तौ" इत्य् अस्मात् परितः सर्वाङ्गे उष्टया कान्तया शोभितया वन-मालया वक्षस्य् एक-देशे वर्तमाना श्रीः संस्पर्धमाना भवति । तथाप्य् आम्नाय-मधुव्रतैर् बहुधा वर्णितया कीर्ति-मय्या वैजयन्त्या वन-मालयैव यो भवान् सुप्रणीतम् अर्हणम् आददद् इत्य्-आदि पूर्ववत् ॥१२॥
word_for_word: among the six groups of servants beginning with sages and Sātvatas
Śrī, as if a rival co-wife
those with growing pure faith in His fame are fulfilled
entries.literal_english: Among the Lord's servants, His affection for the supreme devotees is especially praised. Lakṣmī herself, dwelling on His chest, appears to rival the forest garland offered by devotees, yet He gladly accepts that garland as worship. The commentary also draws the conclusion that those whose pure faith in His fame grows are fulfilled.

entries.sanskrit:
त्वच्-चरणस्य भक्त-पक्ष-पातः प्रसिद्ध एवेति स्तुवन्तः प्रार्थयन्ते---केतुर् इति । बलि-बन्धने त्रिभिर् विक्रमैर् युतः । तत्र द्वितीय-विक्रमे सत्य-लोकं गतस् तव पादः केतुर् अत्युच्छ्रितो विजय-ध्वज इव । तत् सम्पादयन्ति । त्रि-पतत्-पताकः त्रिधा पतन्ती, त्रिषु लोकेषु वा पतन्ती गङ्गा पताका यस्य । तथासुर-देव-चम्वोस् तत् सेनयोर् उभयोर् भयाभय-करः । साधुषु सुरेषु स्वर्गाय खलेष्व् असुरेष्व् इतरायेतरस्मै अधो-गमनाय । य एवं केतु-रूपस् ते पादः स भजतां नोऽघं पुनातु शोधयतु । "अघात्" इति पाठे, भजतां नः इति कर्मणि षष्ठ्यौ । अघाद् भजतोऽस्मान् पुनात्व् इति । तथा च श्रुतिः---

> चरणं पवित्रं विततं पुराणं >
> येन पूतस् तरति दुष्कृतानि । >
> तेन पवित्रेण शुद्धेन पूता >
> अतिपाप्मानम् अरातिं तरेम ॥ \[महानारायणोपनिषद् १.५१\] >
> लोकस्य द्वारम् अर्चिमत्-पवित्रं >
> ज्योतिष्मद्- भ्राजमानं महस्वत् । >
> अमृतस्य धारा बहुधा दोहमानं >
> चरणं नो लोके सुधितां दधातु ॥ इति ॥१३॥
word_for_word: Your foot’s favor toward the side of the devotees
at Bali’s binding, joined with three strides
in the second stride, Your foot reached Satyaloka
it stood very high like a victory-banner
त्रिधा पतन्ती, त्रिषु लोकेषु वा पतन्ती गङ्गा पताका यस्य
whose banner is Gaṅgā, falling in three streams, or falling through the three worlds
for the virtuous gods, toward heaven
for the wicked Asuras, toward the other destination, a downward course
may He purify the sin of us worshippers
bhajatām and naḥ are genitives used with the sense of an object
that is: “May He purify us worshippers from sin”
the foot, holy, widespread, and ancient
by which the purified one crosses misdeeds
purified by that holy, pure purifier
may we cross the exceedingly sinful enemy
yielding streams of nectar in many ways
may that foot establish well-being for us in the world
entries.literal_english: Praising the famed favor shown by Your foot to the devotees, they pray, beginning with “banner.” At Bali’s binding, Your foot took three strides. In the second stride it reached Satyaloka and stood very high, like a victory-banner. The banner is Gaṅgā, falling in three streams or flowing through the three worlds. Your foot brings fear to the Asura army and safety to the Deva army: for the virtuous gods it leads to heaven, and for the wicked Asuras to the other destination, a downward course. May that banner-like foot purify the sin of us worshippers. With the reading “aghāt,” the genitives “bhajatām” and “naḥ” have an object sense: “May He purify us worshippers from sin.” The cited Śruti says: “The foot, holy, widespread, and ancient, by which the purified one crosses misdeeds; purified by that holy, pure purifier, may we cross the exceedingly sinful enemy. The world’s radiant, holy gateway, luminous, shining, and glorious, yielding streams of nectar in many ways—may that foot establish well-being for us in the world.”

entries.sanskrit: ननु युद्धे देवासुरादयः परस्परं जयन्ति, जीयन्ते च किम् अहं तत्रेत्य् अत आहुः---नसीति । मिथुर् मिथोऽर्द्यमाना युद्धादिभिः पीड्यमाना ब्रह्मादयोऽपि यस्य तव वशे भवन्ति, न तु जये पराजये वा स्व-तन्त्राः । के इव ? नसि नासिकायाम् ओता नासिकाम् आविध्य वद्धा गावो बली-वर्दा इव । कुतः ? कालस्य कलयितुः प्रवर्तकस्य । तद् एव कुतः ? प्रकृति-पुरुषयोर् अपि परस्य । तस्य ते पुरुषोत्तमस्य पादो नः शं तनोतु ॥१४॥
word_for_word: ननु युद्धे देवासुरादयः परस्परं जयन्ति, जीयन्ते च
One may object: in battle, Devas and Asuras conquer one another and are conquered
“What have I to do with that?”—therefore they say
mutually assailed and afflicted by battle and the like
even Brahmā and the others are under Your control
न तु जये पराजये वा स्व-तन्त्राः
they are not independent in victory or defeat
नसि नासिकायाम् ओता नासिकाम् आविध्य वद्धा गावो बली-वर्दा इव
like cows and bulls pierced through the nose and tied by a nose-rope
of Time, the reckoner and impeller
who is beyond both Prakṛti and Puruṣa
तस्य ते पुरुषोत्तमस्य पादो नः शं तनोतु
may the foot of You, the Supreme Person, bring us welfare
entries.literal_english: One may object: Devas, Asuras, and the rest conquer one another and are conquered in battle, so what has the Lord to do with it? They answer: even Brahmā and the others, mutually assailed and afflicted by war and other events, are under Your control; they are not independent in victory or defeat. They are like cows and bulls pierced through the nose and tied by a nose-rope. You are Time’s impeller, and You are beyond both Prakṛti and Puruṣa. May the foot of You, the Supreme Person, bring us welfare.

entries.sanskrit:
प्रकृति-पुरुषाभ्यां परत्वम् उपपादयन्तः कालत्वेन पुरुषोत्तमत्वम् आहुः---अस्येति । अस्य जगत उदयादीनां हेतुर् असि । कुतः ? अव्यक्तं प्रकृतिः, जीवः पुरुषः, महान् महत्-तत्त्वं, तेषां कालं नियन्तारं त्वाम् आहुः---

> अक्षरात् परतः परः । महतः परम-व्यक्तम् । अव्यक्तात् पुरुषः > परम् । पुरुषान् न परं किञ्चित् । सा काष्ठा सा परा गतिः ॥ इत्य् > आद्याः श्रुतयः ।

किं च, अयं संवत्सरात्मको यः कालस् त्रिणाभिस् त्रीणि चातुर्-मास्यानि नाभयो यस्य सोऽपि त्वम् एव । अतस् त्वम् उत्तम-पुरुष इति । तथा च गीतासु---

> यस्मात् क्षरम् अतीतोऽहम् अक्षराद् अपि चोत्तमाह् । >
> अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमाह् ॥ \[गीता १५.१८\] इति > ॥१५॥
word_for_word: establishing superiority over Prakṛti and Puruṣa
they state that He is the Supreme Person as Time
You are the cause of this world’s arising and the rest
अव्यक्तं प्रकृतिः, जीवः पुरुषः, महान् महत्-तत्त्वं
the unmanifest is Prakṛti; the Puruṣa is the jīva; the Great is the mahat-tattva
they call You Time, their controller
higher still beyond the imperishable is the Supreme
the unmanifest is higher than the Great
the Puruṣa is higher than the unmanifest
there is nothing higher than the Puruṣa
that is the limit; that is the supreme goal
संवत्सरात्मको यः कालस् त्रिणाभिस् त्रीणि चातुर्-मास्यानि नाभयो यस्य
that Time whose form is the year, whose three hubs are the three four-month periods
therefore You are the Supreme Person
यस्मात् क्षरम् अतीतोऽहम् अक्षराद् अपि चोत्तमाह्
since I transcend the perishable and am higher even than the imperishable
अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमाह्
therefore I am renowned in the world and in the Veda as the Supreme Person
entries.literal_english: Establishing that the Lord is beyond Prakṛti and Puruṣa, they call Him the Supreme Person as Time. “You are the cause of this world’s arising and the rest.” The unmanifest is Prakṛti, the Puruṣa is the jīva, and the Great is the mahat-tattva; the Vedic passages call the Lord Time, the controller of these. They cite the Śruti: “Higher than the Great is the unmanifest; higher than the unmanifest is the Puruṣa; there is nothing higher than the Puruṣa—that is the limit, that is the supreme goal.” They continue: the annual Time, whose three hubs are the three four-month periods, is also the Lord alone; therefore He is the Supreme Person. The Gītā says: “Since I transcend the perishable and am higher even than the imperishable, I am renowned in the world and in the Veda as the Supreme Person.”

entries.sanskrit: त्वम् एव प्रकृत्य्-आदि-द्वारा जगत्-सृष्ट्य्-आदि-द्वारा जगत्-सृष्ट्य्-आदि-हेतुर् इत्य् उक्तम् । तत् केन प्रकारेण ? तद् आहुः---त्वत्त इति । त्वत्तः पुरुषो वीर्यं शक्तिं समधिगम्य प्राप्य यया मायया सह महान्तं धत्ते । कम् इव ? अस्य विश्वस्य गर्भम् इव । सोऽयं महांस् तयैव माययानुगतः सन्न् आत्मनः सकाशाद् आण्ड-कोशं ससर्ज । त्वयऽनुगत इति पाठेऽपि तया मायया त्वयाधिष्ठितः सन्न् इति ॥१६॥
word_for_word: the Puruṣa, obtaining power from You
like the embryo of the universe
entries.literal_english: The Puruṣa receives power from the Lord and, together with māyā, holds the Mahat principle like the embryo of the universe. From that, under the Lord's direction, he creates the golden cosmic egg enclosed by its coverings.

entries.sanskrit: नन्व् एवं-भूतम् ईश्वरत्वं मम कुतोऽवगतं ? तद् आहुः---तद् इति । तत् तस्मात् तस्थूषः स्थावरस्य जगतो जङ्गमस्य च भवान् अधीशः । यद् यस्माद् माययोत्था उज्जृम्भिता या गुण-विक्रिया इन्द्रिय-वृत्तिस् तयोपनीतान् अर्थान् विषयान् जुषन् जुषमाणोऽपि हे हृषीक-पते, न लिप्तस् त्वम् । ये त्व् अन्ये जीवा योगिनो वा स्वतः परिहृताद् अप्य् अविद्यमानात् त्यक्ताद् वा विषय-जोषणाद् बिभ्यति । वासना-मात्रेण बध्यन्त इत्य् अर्थः ॥१७॥
word_for_word: lord of the stationary and moving world
objects brought by the transformations of the guṇas
they are bound merely by latent impressions
entries.literal_english: The Lord is master of all moving and stationary beings. Although He enjoys objects produced by the guṇa transformations, He is not attached to them. Other living beings, even yogins, become bound by latent impressions to objects they have renounced or that are not present.

entries.sanskrit: अलिप्तत्वम् आहुः---स्मायेति । स्मायावलोको मन्द-स्मित-विलसितोऽवलोकः, तस्य लवः कटाक्षः, तेन दर्शितो यो भावोऽभिप्रायः, तेन मनो-हारि यद् भ्रू-मण्डलं, तेन प्रहिता ये सौरता मन्त्राः, तैः शौण्डैः प्रगल्भैर् अनङ्ग-बाणैः कामस्य बाणैः संमोहनैः करणैः काम-कलादिभिः षोडश-सहस्रं पत्न्यो यस्येन्द्रियं मनो विमथितुं क्षोभयितुं न विभ्व्यो न समर्थाः, स भवान् न लिप्त इति पूर्वेणान्वयः ॥१८॥
word_for_word: the feeling shown by a slight smiling glance
were not able to agitate the senses or mind
entries.literal_english: The Lord remains unattached because even the seductive messages conveyed by smiles, side-glances, and arched eyebrows could not agitate Him. His sixteen thousand wives, though capable of serving as Cupid's arrows, could not disturb His senses or mind.

entries.sanskrit: तस्मात् तवामृत-रूपा या कथा, तद् एव उदकं वहन्तीति तथा कीर्ति-नद्यः । तथा पादाव् अनेज-सरितो गङ्गाद्याश् च त्रि-लोक्याः शमलानि हन्तुं विभ्व्यः । केन प्रकारेण ? आनुश्रवं गुरोर् उच्चारणम् अनुश्रूयत इत्य् अनुश्रवो वेदस् तत्र भवं कीर्ति-रूपं तीर्थं श्रुतिभिः श्रवणेन्द्रियैर् अङ्घ्रि-जं चाङ्ग-सङ्गैः । एवं शुचि-षदः स्वाश्रम-धर्म-स्थितास् तव तीर्थ-द्वयम् उपस्पृशन्ति सेवन्त इति ॥१९॥
word_for_word: rivers flowing from the unmoving feet
to destroy the sins of the three worlds
what is heard from the teacher
the sacred ford in the form of fame
entries.literal_english: The Lord's nectar-like stories and the rivers flowing from His feet both cleanse the sins of the three worlds. Pure devotees who remain in their proper āśrama duties approach these two sacred waters: His fame heard through the Veda and teacher, and the foot-born river through bodily contact.
“Together with the gods.”

word_for_word: removing the impurity of all worlds
entries.literal_english: Brahmā says that the Lord fulfilled the earlier request to remove the earth's burden. He established dharma among truthful righteous people and spread His fame throughout the directions, washing away the impurity of all worlds.

entries.sanskrit: उद्दामानि वृत्तानि विक्रमा येषु तानि कर्माणि ।
word_for_word: mighty and unrestrained are the exploits
whose deeds contain such feats of valor
entries.literal_english: The deeds are those in which the exploits are mighty and unrestrained.

entries.literal_english: Without withdrawing the proud Yadu clan, the world would be destroyed by its force overflowing every limit.

entries.sanskrit: प्रभासं यास्याम इति वदतोऽयम् अभिप्रायः---एते देवांशाः स्वाधिकारान् एवार्हन्ति, न तु सद्यो मोक्षम् । द्वारवत्यां मृता मुच्येरंस् तस्माद् अभ्युदय-फल प्रभासं नेष्यामीति ॥३५॥
word_for_word: are entitled to their own offices
those who die in Dvārakā would be liberated
entries.literal_english: The Lord's purpose in sending them to Prabhāsa is that these divine portions may attain their own offices rather than immediate liberation. Those who die in Dvārakā would be liberated, so Prabhāsa is proposed for their elevation.

entries.sanskrit: दक्ष-शापाद् यक्ष्मणा गृहीत उडु-राट् चन्द्रो यत्र स्नान-मात्रं कृत्वा किल्बिषात् तस्माद् रोग-दुःखात् सद्यो विमुक्तः सन् भूयः कला-वृद्धिं भेजे ॥३६॥
word_for_word: seized by consumption through Dakṣa's curse
entries.literal_english: Prabhāsa is the place where the moon, seized by wasting disease through Dakṣa's curse, bathed and was immediately freed from the affliction, after which his lunar phases grew again.

entries.sanskrit: उशिजः कमनीयान् । अन्धसा अन्नेन । उप्त्वेति यथा सुक्षेत्रे बीजम् उप्तं बहु-फलं भवति, तथा दानं सत्-पात्रे इति द्योतयति ॥३७-३८॥
word_for_word: we shall cross the ocean by gifts as by boats
entries.literal_english: At Prabhāsa they will bathe, satisfy the ancestors and gods, feed excellent brāhmaṇas with varied food, and give great gifts to worthy recipients. Charity planted in a worthy field bears abundant fruit and carries them across sin like boats over the ocean.

entries.literal_english: Uddhava recognizes that the Lord is leaving the mortal world. Although He had the power to reverse the brāhmaṇa's curse, He did not obstruct it.

entries.sanskrit: शय्यादिषु त्वां भक्ता नित्यं सेवितवन्तो वयं कथं त्यजेम ॥४५॥
word_for_word: in lying, sitting, walking, staying, bathing, playing, eating, and the like
entries.literal_english: The devotees say that they have constantly served the Lord while lying, sitting, walking, bathing, playing, eating, and in every ordinary activity. How could they abandon Him, their beloved Self?

entries.sanskrit: त्यक्तुम् अशक्नुवन् प्रार्थयते, न माया-भयाद् इत्य् आह---त्वया इति । चर्चिता अलङ्कृताः । हि निश्चितं जयेम ॥४६॥
word_for_word: adorned with garlands, fragrances, clothes, and ornaments used by You
entries.literal_english: Unable to leave Him, they ask to be taken along. Because they wear His garlands, fragrances, clothes, and ornaments and eat His remnants as servants, they are confident that they will conquer māyā.

entries.sanskrit:
संन्यासिनो हि ब्रह्मचर्यादि-क्लेशैः कथञ्चित् तरन्ति, वयं त्व् अनायासेनैव तरिष्याम इत्य् आह---**वात-रशना**[^३१] इति । **ऊर्ध्व-मन्थिन** ऊर्ध्व-रेतसः ॥४७॥

[^३१]: रशना-शब्देन वस्त्रं लक्ष्यते । वाताशनाः इति च पाठः ।
word_for_word: but we shall cross without effort
ūrdhvamanthinaḥ means those whose semen flows upward, celibates
entries.literal_english: Renunciants somehow cross over through hardships beginning with celibacy; “but we shall cross without effort,” says the commentary. It explains “vātaraśanāḥ” as “girdled with wind”: here the word raśanā indicates clothing. The source also records the variant reading “vātāśanāḥ,” “air-eaters.” “Ūrdhvamanthinaḥ” means those whose semen flows upward, that is, celibates.

entries.sanskrit: तावकैर् भक्तैः सह त्वद्-वार्तया दुस्तरं तमः संसारम् । क्ष्वेली परिहासः । द्वन्द्वैकत्वम् ॥४८-४९॥
word_for_word: gait, smiles, glances, and playful acts
entries.literal_english: Together with the Lord's devotees, remembering and recounting His deeds, they will cross the difficult darkness of saṃsāra. The references to gait, smiles, glances, and playful acts are understood as His playful imitation of human life.

entries.sanskrit: एकान्तिनम् इत्य्-आदि स्वाभिप्रायावञ्चने हेतुः ॥५०॥
word_for_word: are the reason for not concealing His own intention
entries.literal_english: The words “single-minded [servant]” and so on explain why the Lord does not conceal His own intention from Uddhava.
